chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from al-Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from al-Washshāʾ, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from Maʿmar ibn Yaḥyā, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
There is no salat (prayer) on the day of al-Fiṭr and al-Aḍḥā except with the Imam.

key_terms.الْأَضْحَى: the festival of sacrifice, ʿĪd al-Aḍḥā
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the Imam whose presence or leadership is required for this prayer in the hadith
key_terms.الْفِطْرِ: the festival marking the end of sawm (fasting), ʿĪd al-Fiṭr
key_terms.صَلَاةَ: the ritual prayer referred to here as the ʿĪd prayer
key_terms.يَوْمَ: the specific day on which the ruling applies

ai.seo_question: Is the ʿĪd prayer valid or obligatory without the Imam?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling that the salat of the two ʿĪds is not established except with the Imam. In context, it indicates the connection of the ʿĪd prayer to legitimate religious authority and communal leadership.
